narration: In the world of supercars, the Audi R8 stands as an icon. At number four, the second-gen R8 V10 RWS enters the fray as a rear-wheel-drive rebel. Starting at $139,900 with 540 hp, it offers a purist twist, focusing on driver engagement. Its unique wheel design and RWS badging set it apart as Audi's daring deviation from the norm. Then Audi introduced the R8 V8 in 2007, turning heads with its iconic side blades and mid-engine layout. At $109,000, this 420 hp marvel laid the foundation for what an Audi supercar could be. Even today, its allure endures, with classic LED headlights and dual exhaust tips defining 'The Original.' Audi turned up the volume with the first-gen R8 V10, delivering 525 hp by 2009. Priced at $146,000, it was a leap forward in performance, though some missed the pure V8 charm. With V10 badging and carbon fiber side blades, it cemented Audi’s place in the supercar league. Topping our list, the second-gen R8 V10 Plus is a masterpiece of engineering. With 610 hp and starting at $189,900, it’s not just about raw power—it’s the driving experience. Its aggressive front grille and fixed rear wing embody the essence of performance. Currently valued at $260K, it's an appreciating blend of speed and sophistication. So, which R8 would you choose to experience—back to the roots with the V8, or all out with the V10 Plus?
